```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(devtools)
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(readr)
library(janitor)
library(here)
library(haven)
library(tigris)
library(tidycensus)
library(purrr)

library(stringr)
library(httr2)
library(jsonlite)

```

```{r Step 0: Data Ingestion, include=TRUE}
cps_wage_analysis <- read_csv(here("01_tidydata", "IPUMS_CPS",
    "cps_wage_analysis_2000_2024.csv"))
```

```{r Step 1, Construct Measure, include=TRUE}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 12a. Start with primary wage-and-salary sample
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cps_wage_premium <- cps_wage_analysis %>%
  filter(worker_type == "Wage and salary") %>%
  mutate(
    
    # Annual hours worked
    annual_hours = weeks_worked_clean * usual_hours_clean,
    
    # Hourly earnings
    hourly_wage = wage_income_clean / annual_hours,
    
    # Log hourly earnings
    log_hourly_wage = log(hourly_wage)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    is.finite(hourly_wage),
    hourly_wage > 0,
    is.finite(log_hourly_wage)
  )


# ============================================================
# 13. ESTIMATE YEAR-SPECIFIC INDUSTRY WAGE PREMIUMS
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 13a. Prepare covariates
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cps_wage_premium <- cps_wage_premium %>%
  mutate(
    
    # Convert labelled variables to factors for regression
    sex_factor = factor(sex),
    race_factor = factor(race),
    region_factor = factor(region),
    educ_factor = factor(educ_category),
    
    # Potential experience and quadratic term
    experience = potential_experience,
    experience_sq = potential_experience^2
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 13b. Estimate year-specific industry wage models
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Model:
#
# log(hourly wage) =
#     education
#   + potential experience
#   + potential experience^2
#   + sex
#   + race
#   + region
#   + industry
#
# Industry coefficients represent adjusted wage premiums
# relative to the omitted industry category.

industry_wage_models <- cps_wage_premium %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  group_map(
    ~ feols(
        log_hourly_wage ~
          educ_factor +
          experience +
          experience_sq +
          sex_factor +
          race_factor +
          region_factor |
          industry,
        data = .x,
        weights = ~asecwt_clean
      )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 13c. Extract industry fixed effects
# ------------------------------------------------------------

industry_premiums <- lapply(
  seq_along(industry_wage_models),
  function(i) {
    
    model <- industry_wage_models[[i]]
    
    # Identify the year corresponding to this model
    model_data <- cps_wage_premium %>%
      filter(year == sort(unique(cps_wage_premium$year))[i])
    
    year_i <- unique(model_data$year)
    
    # Extract industry fixed effects
    fe <- fixef(model)$industry
    
    tibble(
      year = year_i,
      industry = as.integer(names(fe)),
      industry_premium = as.numeric(fe)
    )
  }
) %>%
  bind_rows()


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 13d. Center premiums within year
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# The raw fixed effects are relative to the omitted industry.
# Centering them around the weighted industry mean makes the
# resulting measure easier to interpret as a relative premium.

industry_weights <- cps_wage_premium %>%
  group_by(year, industry) %>%
  summarise(
    industry_weight = sum(asecwt_clean, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

industry_premiums <- industry_premiums %>%
  left_join(
    industry_weights,
    by = c("year", "industry")
  ) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  mutate(
    weighted_mean_premium = weighted.mean(
      industry_premium,
      w = industry_weight,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    industry_wage_premium = industry_premium - weighted_mean_premium
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(
    year,
    industry,
    industry_wage_premium
  )


# ============================================================
# 14. SAVE INDUSTRY-LEVEL WAGE PREMIUM
# ============================================================

saveRDS(
  industry_premiums,
  here::here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "IPUMS_CPS",
    "CPS_IndustryWagePremium_2000_2024.rds"
  )
)

write.csv(
  industry_premiums,
  here::here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "IPUMS_CPS",
    "CPS_IndustryWagePremium_2000_2024.csv"
  ),
  row.names = FALSE
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 14a. Basic diagnostics
# ------------------------------------------------------------

summary(industry_premiums$industry_wage_premium)

industry_premiums %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    n_industries = n(),
    mean_premium = weighted.mean(
      industry_wage_premium,
      w = industry_weight,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    sd_premium = sd(industry_wage_premium, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_premium = min(industry_wage_premium, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_premium = max(industry_wage_premium, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```
